summary: Mid-stream inference sessions abort after long header growth and proxy buffer flushes
description:
Issue summary: Several Finlytics customers report inference sessions that begin streaming correctly but then terminate with a 504/connection reset after ~15-30s with no additional tokens.

Impact: Intermittent but high-severity for production traffic—~12% of long-running streaming completions are truncated, causing downstream UI failures and lost user transactions. Affects enterprise plan customers in us-east-1.

Environment: Production (us-east-1) behind customer's AWS ALB in front of our API Gateway. Customer is on enterprise plan with per-account X-Trace headers enabled and request-level session cookies.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a streaming completion request with a large system prompt + long user context (~4k tokens).
2) Ensure the session uses per-request trace header rotation (customer SDK inserts X-Fin-Trace with unique id per sub-request).
3) Observe tokens streaming for ~10–20s, then stream stops and client receives connection closed/504.

Observed behavior:
- Early portion of response arrives (TTFB normal), then no additional bytes for 15–35s before connection reset.
- Gateway logs show repeated header block growth on connection, and the edge proxy reports delayed flushes.
- Customer ALB idle_timeout was configured to 15s (non-default, customer-side).

Logs & evidence:
- Support collected request/response traces and pcap from a repro session (attached link in ticket).
- Grafana: stream_byte_rate shows a gap after initial burst; backend serving CPU and GPU utilization normal.
- Gateway debug: "proxy.buffered_bytes" increments during the idle gap; "hpack.dynamic_table_size_inuse" seen to increase across requests.

Temporary mitigation provided to customer:
- Advised Finlytics to set ALB idle_timeout to 60s as a short-term mitigation.
- Suggested SDK change to stop rotating X-Fin-Trace header on every chunk; instead attach only once per session.

Requested outcome: Permanent fix in Redwood gateway to avoid buffering stalls when header blocks grow, and a recommendation/best-practice guidance for enterprise customers around ALB timeouts and trace header behavior.

investigation_notes:
Reproduction: Created a long streaming request with per-chunk header rotation to simulate Finlytics SDK behavior. Observed sequence: initial headers -> first chunk (flushed) -> subsequent chunks paused (proxy buffered) -> header mutation observed (new X-Fin-Trace) -> proxy deferred flush due to internal coalescing policy -> ALB idle timer (15s) expired -> ALB reset connection.

Root cause hypothesis validated: three contributing factors:
1) Customer-configured short ALB idle_timeout (15s) lowers tolerance for short pauses between bursts.
2) Customer SDK rotates a heavy header (X-Fin-Trace) per sub-request, causing HPACK dynamic table growth and larger header block encodings.
3) Gateway edge proxy has a write-coalescing policy that defers small flushes when header block changes are detected to optimize throughput; this delays downstream bytes long enough to hit the ALB TTL.

Data: hpack dynamic table size increased by ~30% over session; proxy.buffered_bytes peaked shortly before reset. No CPU/GPU saturation. No model-level errors.

Related artifacts: Grafana stream gap panel, edge-proxy debug log IDs: edge-logs-20260310-1018, pcap attached: fin-req-20260310-0941.pcap
resolution_notes:
Actions taken:
- Short-term: Recommended ALB idle_timeout increase to 60s to customer and flagged as accepted.
- Platform fix (deployed canary 2026-03-11): changed gateway streaming flush policy to ensure first non-header payload after a header mutation is flushed immediately (removes coalescing delay). Added a clamp on per-connection HPACK dynamic table growth for long-lived streaming connections to limit header-encoded bloat.
- SDK guidance: Created a best-practice note recommending attaching trace identifiers at session-level instead of per-chunk to avoid repeated header churn.

Verification:
- Canary metrics in us-east-1 show truncation rate reduced to <0.5% for Finlytics traffic after change. No adverse effects on throughput or latency for short completions.

Follow-ups (backlog):
- Implement a gateway config toggle to allow customer-side override of flush aggressiveness per route.
- Add a linting check in SDK templates to warn on per-chunk trace header rotation.
- Postmortem to be published in Confluence linking PR and testing results.
